title: Accelerating Transformer Inference with Structured State Space Models
problem: Transformer inference suffers from high memory footprint and computational overhead during deployment. Existing approaches struggle to balance model capacity with inference efficiency.
motivation: Efficient inference is critical for deploying large language models at scale in resource-constrained environments.
method: The approach combines transformer attention mechanisms with structured state space models (SSMs) to reduce state representation overhead. SSMs enable efficient sequential modeling through compressed state management while maintaining the expressiveness of attention, reducing memory consumption during inference.
key_novelty: Integration of structured state space models with transformer attention mechanisms to simultaneously achieve memory efficiency and inference accuracy.
contributions: 45% reduction in memory footprint compared to baseline transformers
Novel hybrid architecture combining SSMs with transformer attention
Maintains accuracy on language modeling benchmarks while improving efficiency
limitations: Specific speedup metrics, hardware deployment results, and comparison with other efficient inference methods not discussed in abstract.
